title: JPMorgan CEO Jamie Dimon says the AI spending boom is likely to pay off
excerpt: Jamie Dimon said spending on data centers has boosted the US economy, creating jobs and demand for construction materials.
content_html:
Jamie Dimon is optimistic that the country's AI spending will pay off.

The JPMorgan CEO told CNBC's Leslie Picker in a video interview that aired on Wednesday that he believes the billions pouring into AI infrastructure will ultimately prove worthwhile.

"In my own view, and I may be wrong, it'll ultimately play out and pay out," Dimon said. "These people are doing real calculations about what's needed. They see what it costs to do the frontier models. They see what it costs to do inferencing. The need is going up dramatically."

He said that AI spending is also driving the American economy, "because the increase alone is 1% of GDP, and next year it's going to be another 1% of GDP increase."

"You've got to get steel and cement and all these things to build the data centers," he added.

When asked about whether a cooling AI market would be a threat to the nation's economy, Dimon said that while there are "a lot of things to worry about," this specific scenario is "not high on the list."

JPMorgan has poured significant capital into tech and AI projects this year, with Dimon saying on a January earnings call that he didn't want the bank to fall behind other Wall Street rivals and fintech companies.

"We are going to stay out front, so help us God," he said in response to a question about the bank's spending from Wells Fargo analyst Mike Mayo.

The bank then announced in February that it was planning to boost its technology budget to $19.8 billion this year, which included investments in some AI projects.

Since then, the company has pushed its engineers to use AI more, tracking their usage on internal dashboards. Business Insider saw screenshots of some of these tracking systems and spoke to current and former developers, most of whom were worried about being labeled as underperformers if their AI use didn't increase.

During a second-quarter earnings call in July, Dimon said that AI has led to as much as a 40% reduction in jobs in some areas of the firm, but that it wouldn't suddenly shrink its operational budget.

But that's not to say he hasn't been skeptical about high AI spending, particularly in recent months, as the tokenmaxxing trend has been on the decline. In July, the executive said during a CNBC appearance that companies need to be rational about AI spending, "like any other resource we use."

The company's AI leadership is also undergoing a reset following the July announcement by its AI chief, Teresa Heitsenrether, that she would retire after four decades at the bank.

content_html_zh:
杰米·戴蒙 (Jamie Dimon) 乐观地认为，该国的人工智能支出将会得到回报。

这位摩根大通首席执行官在周三播出的视频采访中告诉 CNBC 的莱斯利·皮克 (Leslie Picker)，他相信投入人工智能基础设施的数十亿美元最终将被证明是值得的。

“在我看来，也许我是错的，它最终会发挥作用并得到回报，”戴蒙说。 “这些人正在对需要什么进行真正的计算。 他们看到了开发前沿模型的成本。 他们看到进行推理的成本。 需求正在急剧增加。”

他表示，人工智能支出也在推动美国经济，“因为仅增长就占GDP的1%，明年将再增长1%。”

“你必须获得钢铁和水泥以及所有这些东西来建造数据中心，”他补充道。

当被问及人工智能市场降温是否会对国家经济构成威胁时，戴蒙表示，虽然“有很多事情需要担心”，但这种具体情况“并不是最重要的”。

摩根大通今年向科技和人工智能项目投入了大量资金，戴蒙在 1 月份的财报电话会议上表示，他不希望该银行落后于其他华尔街竞争对手和金融科技公司。

在回答富国银行分析师迈克·梅奥有关该银行支出的问题时，他表示：“我们将保持领先地位，所以请上帝帮助我们。”

该银行随后于 2 月份宣布，计划将今年的技术预算增加至 198 亿美元，其中包括对一些人工智能项目的投资。

从那时起，该公司就推动工程师更多地使用人工智能，并在内部仪表板上跟踪他们的使用情况。 《商业内幕》看到了其中一些跟踪系统的屏幕截图，并与现任和前任开发人员进行了交谈，他们中的大多数人担心，如果他们的人工智能使用不增加，就会被贴上表现不佳的标签。

在 7 月份的第二季度财报电话会议上，戴蒙表示，人工智能已导致公司某些领域的工作岗位减少了 40%，但不会突然缩减运营预算。

但这并不是说他对人工智能的高额支出不持怀疑态度，尤其是最近几个月，因为代币最大化趋势一直在下降。 今年 7 月，这位高管在接受 CNBC 采访时表示，公司需要对人工智能支出保持理性，“就像我们使用的任何其他资源一样”。

继 7 月份人工智能主管 Teresa Heitsenrether 宣布她将在银行工作 40 年后退休后，该公司的人工智能领导层也正在经历重新调整。
